0.1.n: This English loanword forms the first part of the title スクールロマンス.

0.2.n: This English loanword forms the second part of the title スクールロマンス.

0.5.n: Repeating まだ emphasizes that the series has plenty more to come.

0.6.n: This points to the time ahead, starting now.

0.7.n: After これから, も suggests the series will continue in the future just as it has until now.

0.8.n: 続く becomes 続いて and joins いきます, politely describing continuation into the future.

0.9.n: This connects the series continuing with the speaker’s following hope for viewers.

1.0.n: This adds emphasis to the question, expressing strong curiosity rather than anger here.

1.1.n: This asks what direction the story will take.

1.2.n: なる becomes なって and joins いく to describe change unfolding over time.

1.3.n: Before か, の frames the question as something the speaker is wondering about.

1.4.n: This marks the preceding words as an embedded question about how the story will develop.

1.6.n: Here it refers to the unfolding plot, rather than development in a general sense.

1.7.n: This marks the story developments as what causes the viewers’ excited feelings.

1.8.n: This sound-like expression describes suspense or nervous excitement and shares し with ワクワク here.

1.10.n: This describes eager, happy excitement about what happens next.

1.11.n: This is the linking form of する, turning the excitement expressions into an action before ながら.

1.12.n: Attached to し, this shows that feeling excited and enjoying the series happen at the same time.

1.14.n: This combines with に to describe enjoying the series alongside others.

1.15.n: This makes 一緒 describe how viewers enjoy the series.

1.16.n: 楽しむ becomes 楽しんで and joins くださる, respectfully presenting viewers’ enjoyment as something appreciated by the speaker.

1.17.n: This introduces the condition that would make the speaker happy.

1.18.n: This describes how the speaker would feel if viewers enjoyed the series together.

1.19.n: The stretched な adds a warm, reflective tone to the speaker’s wish.

1.21.n: This marks the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

1.22.n: This is the polite form of 思う, softening the expression of the speaker’s hope.

2.0.n: This signals a transition to the closing remarks.

2.1.n: This announces the end of the speaker’s message.

2.8.n: After a character name, this identifies the character the performer plays.

2.10.n: This is the first segment of the name つぐは, not a separate word here.

2.11.n: Here は completes the name つぐは; it is not the topic particle.

2.12.n: This is the first part of でした, the polite past form of です.

2.13.n: This completes でした, used here in a conventional sign-off identifying the speaker.

3.0.n: This combines with ございました to make a polite expression of gratitude.

3.1.n: This is part of ございます, which makes ありがとう more formal and respectful.

3.2.n: This is the form of the polite ending ます used before the past ending た.

3.3.n: This completes ありがとうございました, thanking the audience for something already done, such as listening.

0.lit: School Romance, still much more, from now on too, will keep continuing, so…
0.tip: Verb て-form plus いく describes something continuing or developing into the future.

1.lit: How on earth will it develop? While excited at developments, if you kindly enjoy together, I think I’d be happy.
1.tip: 楽しんでくださると嬉しい expresses a warm hope: the speaker would be happy if viewers enjoyed it.

2.lit: Well then, that is all; playing ???, this was Tsuguha!
2.tip: つぐは is the speaker’s name, so its は is not a particle.

3.lit: Thank you very much for what you have done!
3.tip: ありがとうございました is a polite thank-you for something already completed, often used when closing a message.
